name: 3-CMC
addictionPotential: 3-CMC may lead to compulsive redosing and habitual use; formal dependence data are not provided.
toxicities: Ten deaths confirmed by biological samples; six involved polydrug use, so those cases do not isolate 3-CMC's contribution.
effectsSummary: Anecdotal reports describe stimulant and entactogenic effects, with possible cardiovascular symptoms, compulsive redosing and psychosis. Effects are not reliably predictable, and these reports are anecdotal.
dosageRemark: The user-reported dose and duration tables are for education, not as recommendations. Because confirmed deaths are reported and high doses and insufflation are strongly discouraged, numeric dose tiers were not transcribed.
generalRisks: Of potential serious injury or death. It cites neurotoxicity in mice and anecdotal cardiovascular and neurological symptoms after frequent or high-dose use; human risk estimates remain uncertain.
saferUse: The page strongly recommends avoiding 3-CMC; it also warns against high doses, insufflation and redosing, and advises harm-reduction measures.
metabolism: Human hepatocyte and case-sample work identified ketone reduction, N-demethylation and carboxylation. Complete enzyme contributions and clinical elimination kinetics remain undetermined.
summary: 3-CMC is a synthetic chlorinated cathinone described as a stimulant and entactogen. Information about its pharmacology and risks remains limited.
